default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-608.title: Cumulative lower/upper wick pressure follow
E-608.hypothesis: Over a window, lower wicks much larger than upper wicks mean dips were repeatedly bought by passive liquidity that keeps absorbing; follow that side when the net wick share crosses a threshold.

E-609.title: Session-midpoint dwell reclaim follow
E-609.hypothesis: After the price spent a while on one side of the developing day-range midpoint, the first close back across it marks the balance area being re-accepted and rotation usually continues across; follow.

E-610.title: Clock-hour open dwell reclaim follow
E-610.hypothesis: Hourly opens are anchors for desks that scale by the hour; after staying on one side of this hour's open, a close back across it shows flow from that hour's participants switching; follow.

E-611.title: Volume-weighted close vs mean close follow
E-611.hypothesis: When the volume-weighted mean close of a window sits above its simple mean, contracts traded at the higher prices: informed size is buying up; follow when the standardised gap crosses a threshold.

E-612.title: Narrowest-range bar break (Crabel NR-n)
E-612.hypothesis: A bar with the smallest range of the last n bars shows participants stepping aside; the next bar closing beyond its extreme releases stored energy in that direction; follow.

E-613.title: Afternoon trend-day EMA-cross fade
E-613.hypothesis: After a morning that moved more than usual, afternoon liquidity is thin and trend followers have already positioned; a close back through a medium EMA against the day shows exhaustion; fade the day.

E-614.title: Session volume-climax bar fade
E-614.hypothesis: The largest-volume bar of the session so far, with volume well above normal for the minute, is where the impatient side exhausts itself; the next move reverts against that bar's colour.

E-615.title: Prior-session VWAP reclaim follow
E-615.hypothesis: Yesterday's final VWAP is the average price of the whole day's inventory; after trading on one side of it for a while, a close back across means yesterday's holders are in or out of the money again; follow.

E-616.title: Return versus same minute yesterday follow
E-616.hypothesis: Price versus its level at the same clock minute of the previous session measures the speed of the day-over-day drift that funds benchmark against; follow when the gap exceeds its usual size.

E-617.title: Midday box break follow
E-617.hypothesis: The 12:00 lunch window is a low-liquidity balance; the first close beyond its range after the box ends shows afternoon (US-open) flow taking control; follow the break.
